# GitHub source

The `github` type reads one repository's issues and pull requests.
It does not read the repository's files or commits; the `workspace-graph`
[profile](../profiles/index.md) does. The first four sections match what
`okg deployment source-types` prints.

<!-- source-type:start (generated by scripts/render_source_type_pages.py) -->
## What it reads

Reads the issues and pull requests of one repository through your GitHub CLI login.

Record types it adds: `issue`, `pull_request`, `repo`.

## Settings

| Setting | Required | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repository` | yes |  | Repository as owner/name. |
| `include_discussion` | no | `false` | Also read issue and review comments. |

## Access

Reuses your existing GitHub CLI login (`gh auth login`); no token is copied or saved.

## Updates and removals

An edited record is detected by the service's update marker and updates the same graph record.
A record that is missing after a complete, successful scan is removed from the next published version. A scan that stops early or fails removes nothing.
Refreshes when you run `okg ingest --deployment <name>` or when the deployment's scheduled refresh runs; every refresh re-reads the whole repository.
<!-- source-type:end -->

## Add it

Log in to the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) once with
`gh auth login`, then preview:

```bash
okg deployment add-source <name> issues --type github \
  --setting repository=<owner>/<repo>
```

Run it again with `--apply --yes` to add the source.

## Check it

```bash
okg search --deployment <name> --query '<a word from an issue title>'
```

An issue is named `issue:github:<owner>/<repo>:#<number>` and a pull
request `pr:github:<owner>/<repo>:#<number>`. Text from GitHub is marked
`⟦UNTRUSTED_DATA source=<name>.issues⟧` in results, so an agent treats it as
data, not as instructions.

## When it fails

- `no authorized GitHub CLI session`: run `gh auth login`, then retry.
- `gh: Not Found (HTTP 404)`: the repository name is wrong, or your GitHub
  login cannot see it.
- `producer_node_subtype_not_allowed` at the import step: in this version,
  `include_discussion=true` fails this way. Leave it off: remove the failed
  source and add it again without that setting.
- Any other failed step: see
  [If a step fails](index.md#connect-the-source).
